title: Sorting a Linen Closet
description: Group folded bedding and towels on cupboard shelves.
cardDescription: Group folded bedding and towels on cupboard shelves.
focus: The setting is sorting a Linen Closet. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Soft support for the head in bed
Large soft covering used for warmth
Movable panel at a room's entrance
Soft fiber used for many shirts and towels

answerNotes.SHEET: Sheet can name paper, bed linen, or a flat baking pan. The scene tells whether the material is paper, cloth, or metal.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.COTTON: Cotton is a plant fiber used in many washable household items. Wool instead comes from an animal's fleece.

description: Divide eating and cooking tools into spaces in a kitchen drawer.
cardDescription: Divide eating and cooking tools into spaces in a kitchen drawer.
focus: The setting is a Kitchen Drawer for Utensils. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Tool such as a spoon or spatula
Pull-out compartment in a piece of furniture
Utensil with a small bowl at one end
Paired gripping tool used to lift food
Partition used to keep groups of objects apart
Part held when carrying or using something
Material such as iron or copper
Flat serving container with a raised edge

answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides in and out of furniture. Its front may have a handle, while dividers separate the contents inside.
answerNotes.FORK: A fork's prongs hold pieces of food. A garden fork is a larger tool sharing that pronged shape.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.KNIFE: A knife cuts with a blade. In the kitchen, the board beneath the food supports the ingredient while it is sliced.
answerNotes.WHISK: A whisk's loops help mix liquids and beat in air. It works differently from a flat spatula used to lift or turn food.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.

Flat playing surface inside a game box
One playing piece from a deck
One separate part of a whole
Small object representing a player or position
Instruction governing how a game is played
Place in a neat vertical pile
Round piece moved in a familiar board game

answerNotes.GAME: Game names the organized activity or contest. Equipment such as a bat or board is used in the game but is not the game itself.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.PIECE: A piece is one part of a whole. Matching shape, color, and edges helps a jigsaw piece fit its correct place.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.

answerNotes.SHOE: A shoe's sole is its bottom surface. The upper covers the foot, and the heel is the raised or rear part.
answerNotes.BOOT: A boot rises above the ankle. Its sole can leave a tread pattern in mud or snow.
answerNotes.SOLE: The sole is the shoe's bottom. The tread is the pattern on its outer surface that contacts the ground.
answerNotes.LACE: A shoelace threads through openings to fasten a shoe. Lace can also name decorative openwork fabric, a different sense.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.BRUSH: A brush holds many bristles in one handle. Their width and stiffness affect the marks or cleaning action it makes.

answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
answerNotes.SHIRT: A shirt has separate parts such as a collar, sleeves, and cuffs. Naming the part helps distinguish it from the whole garment.
answerNotes.HAT: A hat covers the head. The brim projects outward, while the crown is the part above it.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
